title: Multiplying and dividing algebraic terms
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:19Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches multiplying or dividing algebraic terms: the fractions point covers numeric fractions, like terms covers adding and subtracting, and expanding brackets covers a term times a sum, so a new point is needed.

draft.title: Multiplying and dividing algebraic terms
card: To multiply terms, multiply the numbers first, then the pronumerals. So \(3a \times 4b = 12ab\).
Same pronumerals multiply to a power: \(a \times a = a^{2}\). So \(2x \times 5x = 10x^{2}\).
To divide terms, write them as a fraction and cancel common factors from the top and bottom.
Example: \(12xy \div 4x = \frac{12xy}{4x}\). Divide 12 by 4 to get 3, and cancel \(x\), leaving \(3y\).
draft.remember: Multiply numbers then pronumerals. To divide, cancel like a fraction.

a.why: Multiply the numbers: \(5 \times 2 = 10\). Then the pronumerals: \(m \times n = mn\). Adding the numbers to get \(7mn\) mixes up multiplying with adding.
a.clue: Multiply the numbers, then write the letters together.

b.why: Write \(\frac{18ab}{6b}\). Divide 18 by 6 to get 3, and cancel \(b\), leaving \(3a\). The answer \(3ab\) forgets that \(b\) is on the bottom as well.
b.clue: Which pronumeral appears on both the top and the bottom?
